pressures.name: Anthrax outbreak in DR Congo wildlife

chair.lede: We hold the clock at 85.0 seconds, with the single biggest concern being the surge of extreme weather events across multiple regions.
body: Flash flooding in the U.S. Southwest and Colorado, combined with a second cyclone threatening India, represent new climate‑driven hazards not covered in the baseline.
An anthrax outbreak killing hippos in the Virunga National Park highlights a novel zoonotic risk linked to drought and conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Cyber‑enabled fake emergency alerts about nuclear and chemical threats in Ukraine and Russia demonstrate a fresh AI‑driven vulnerability.
These developments collectively add modest pressure but do not yet warrant moving the clock.

experts.say: No new nuclear weapon tests, treaty changes, or substantive escalation reported; the items are drills, partnership talks, and cyber‑alert hoaxes, which do not add fresh danger.

Flash flooding in the Southwest and Colorado and a second cyclone threatening India highlight new extreme weather events, while the anthrax outbreak linked to drought in DR Congo (10) shows climate‑driven wildlife threats. Additionally, US Democrats shifting climate policy focus to energy bills (18) signals a rollback of climate action.
Anthrax outbreak kills hippos in DR Congo’s Virunga National Park, highlighting a new zoonotic disease flare-up that could threaten wildlife and human health.

Recent cyberattacks spoofed emergency alert apps in Ukraine and Russia, sending false nuclear and chemical warnings, indicating a new misuse of AI‑enabled disinformation tools and a fresh vulnerability in critical infrastructure.
No new war, treaty collapse, or major incident emerged; existing ceasefire lapses and cyber alerts are continuations of ongoing tensions (e.g., 12,24,21).
